newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan exchange dormant at end of weekly trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordan exchange dormant at end of weekly trade.

text.p: Jordan's stock exchange closed almost unchanged at the end of weekly trade on Wednesday in dormant trade, dealers said.
Shares worth 295,436 dinars ($417,282) changed hands, down from 426,000 dinars on Tuesday.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose a marginal 0.05 points to 147.74 points, its first rise after an eighth consecutive daily fall with the market spending the day rangebound.
"The activity was on a few stocks..the market needs major factors to improve it and its still suffering from a liquidity crunch," one broker said.

The exchange, blighted by high domestic interest rates and worries over barriers to trade with sanction-hit Iraq to the east and with Israel and the Palestinian territories to the west, has traded in a tight range since early October.
Blue-chip Arab Bank Group accounted for nearly a third of the total turnover, worth nearly 103,350 dinars, with a 0.5 dinars rise to close at 246.50 dinars.
Aside from Housing Bank the second most active stock with 50,655 dinars worth of trade, the market lacked any buying impetus with negligible purchasing power across the board.
Blue-chip Intermediate Petrochemical and Chemical was the top price gainer with a 4.26 percent rise to 0.98 dinars in low 4,750 shares changing hands.
Overall, nine shares declined with only seven advancing, while 17 traded but closed unchanged.
